Codrington College, on the east coast of Barbados, opened in 1745 under the will of Christopher Codrington, a planter and governor who died in 1710. It is the oldest Anglican theological college in the western hemisphere.

Codrington left two sugar estates, with the enslaved people on them, to the Church of England's missionary society. The estates paid for the college, so a church school was funded by slave labour, and the society even branded its slaves.

The college still trains clergy for the Caribbean church. In 2006 the Church of England apologised for its part in slavery, and the Codrington estates are often cited in debates on reparations, as is the family's Betty's Hope in Antigua.
